newsitem.title: UK: Energy Q1 profit down, takes windfall charge.
newsitem.headline: Energy Q1 profit down, takes windfall charge.

text.p: The Energy Group Plc, whose plans to merge with Pacificorp have hit a regulatory hurdle, said on Wednesday that it made first quarter operating profit of 96 million pounds ($151.6 million), down two percent on the same quarter in 1996.
The British electricity company also said it has taken a one off provision of 112 million pounds for the British government's windfall levy.

Chancellor Gordon Brown imposed the one-off tax in the budget on July 2 and plans to raise around 2.1 billion pounds from the electricity sector, some 1.65 billion from water companies and another 1.45 billion from other privatised utilities.

Energy said that underlying profit for the three months to June 30, 1997 was 14 percent above the same period last year. However, operating profit slipped slightly after absorbing about 20 million pounds of seasonal losses on UK coal-fired power stations.
Turnover in the three month period rose by 19 percent to 1.03 billion pounds.
"Our core businesses are continuing to perform strongly and we are pleased with the initial contribution from our new investments," said chairman Derek Bonham.

Britain's Department of Trade and Industry said on August 1 it was referring the planned acquisition of Energy by U.S.-based PacifiCorp to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission. The DTI's referral came two days after PacifiCorp said it had received acceptances representing 61.6 percent of Energy under its agreed 3.7 billion pounds bid for the company.
